summary.intent: Ship Phase 67 (tee-lease-renewer-contract-rewrite) by running the full post-execute-phase loop autonomously: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit → ship → resolve PR reviews → extract learnings.
summary.outcome: Completed through simplify + SDK E2E gate. SECURITY.md and VALIDATION.md written, dead code removed, migration guard hardened in e2e beforeAll, all tests green. Transcript cuts off before CodeRabbit, PR creation, review resolution, and learnings extraction.

repo: Phase 67 replaced `signIpnsRecord` with `renewIpnsRecord` as the active IPNS signing primitive; `signIpnsRecord` became dead code (only self-referenced) after the phase and was safe to delete.

`tee_key_state` table is empty on a fresh DB and gets populated by `initializeFromTee()` at API startup only when the tee-worker is healthy and secrets match — must start API fresh with correct env to see rows.
Root SECURITY.md is a pre-existing tracked GitHub Security Policy (from #482), not created by the GSD security auditor; it was untouched throughout the run.
The secure-phase enforcement hook was inactive (`activeHooks: []`) for this project, meaning GSD would not hard-block advancement — the ship-phase script required the audit anyway.
ASVS level = 1, block_on = high from project config; 24/24 threats across 8 plans were CLOSED by the auditor (all plans had `<threat_model>` blocks → `register_authored_at_plan_time: true`).
Phase 67 commit subjects were already conventional (`type(67-NN):` format) — the filter-branch reword step was a no-op.

The tee-republish sdk-e2e suite's `beforeAll` did not assert the `information_schema` column-drop, meaning CI could pass against an un-migrated schema; this was a non-blocking auditor finding that was fixed inline.
All sdk-e2e test defaults resolve to the local stack (API_URL→:3000, SECRET→harness default, throttle bypass optional) without explicit env overrides.

code.finding: `signIpnsRecord` and its orphaned JSDoc were dead code after the phase — the route exclusively used `renewIpnsRecord`. Removed safely; tee-worker typecheck + 74 tests still pass.
Added `information_schema` column-drop assertion to `beforeAll` so CI will fail fast against an un-migrated schema rather than silently passing.

workflow: Build chain order for SDK E2E gate must be: crypto → core → api-client → sdk-core → sdk → api — rebuilding only a subset leaves dist out of sync with CI.
Always restart the API fresh (kill by lsof PID, re-launch with full env) before e2e runs; a stale API process from a previous session has unknown env and an older dist.

When ASVS=1 and all threats are pre-planned (register_authored_at_plan_time: true), the workflow allows a short-circuit skip of the auditor — but for TEE/key-lifecycle phases it is worth running the auditor anyway to get concrete code-line evidence.
Run targeted unit suites (tee-worker, api republish+tee specs, sdk-core registration) rather than the full monorepo to validate coverage without RAM contention.

The two-test tee-republish e2e suite (Test A: renewed record preserves CID+seq, extends EOL; Test B: tombstoned name never re-signed) is the only gate that exercises the real client→API IPNS round-trip for this phase's change surface.

friction: The running API (PID 85464) predated the rebuild and had unknown env, requiring a kill + fresh restart with explicit env vars before e2e could be trusted.
apps/api/.env had no THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET key, requiring investigation of the suite's env contract before wiring the correct invocation.
The gsd-secure-phase enforcement hook was inactive, creating ambiguity about whether GSD would actually gate advancement — had to proceed on the ship-phase script's explicit requirement instead.
Removing dead `signIpnsRecord` required two separate Edit calls (function body + orphaned JSDoc) because the JSDoc was not contiguous with the function in the file.
The validate-phase skill loaded but the workflow was not fully exercised via the subagent path — gap analysis and auditor spawn were done inline instead, requiring manual gap cross-referencing.
